title: Portfolio Completion Plan — Fix, Polish, 100% Coverage
description: Complete the portfolio website with all fixes, polish, and validation to achieve 100% coverage across tests, linting, type checking, react-doctor, and accessibility. Ensure profile images from Sanity display correctly in all components including the chatbot UI (FloatingHub, HubMenu, ChatPanel).
objectives: Fix streaming SSR data flow so FloatingHub/ChatPanel/HubMenu display profile image, name, and title from Sanity
Achieve 100/100 react-doctor score and maintain it across all changes
Ensure all TypeScript strict checks pass (tsc --noEmit)
Ensure all ESLint rules pass (npm run lint)
Ensure all 1004+ existing tests pass (npm run test -- --run)
Profile image renders correctly in HubMenu, ChatPanel header, empty state, and hero section
Name and title render correctly in all chatbot UI components
Verify Sanity content completeness for profile, hero, social links

architecture.overview: The portfolio uses Next.js 16 App Router with two data-fetching modes: (1) Streaming SSR — individual sections fetch their own data via SectionProvider context, and (2) Full SSR — all data fetched via getCmsContent() at the layout level. The FloatingHub component lives in the layout and consumes the root CmsContent context. In streaming SSR mode, hero/profile data was missing from the root context, causing the chatbot UI to show empty fallback values. The fix adds fetchHeroData() to the layout's streaming SSR path and merges profile, hero, and socialLinks into the root context.

dataFlow.before: layout.tsx (streaming SSR) → streamingCmsContent (only seoSettings + fallback) → Providers → CmsContentProvider → FloatingHub → useCmsContent() → empty hero/profileImageUrl, name, title
dataFlow.after: layout.tsx (streaming SSR) → fetchSeoData() + fetchHeroData() → streamingCmsContent (seoSettings + hero/profile/socialLinks + fallback) → Providers → CmsContentProvider → FloatingHub → useCmsContent() → real hero data with profileImageUrl, name, title
dataFlow.nonStreaming: getCmsContent() already fetches everything — no change needed
